exampleSentences.en: Tiny lights were glittering across the harbor as we walked home.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們走回家時，點點燈光在港灣上閃爍。

exampleSentences.en: Despite the candidate's glittering résumé, the selection panel questioned his lack of practical experience.
exampleSentences.zh: 儘管候選人的履歷光鮮亮眼，遴選委員會仍質疑他缺乏實務經驗。

glittering.mnemonicHint: glitter 讓人聯想到亮粉一閃一閃；加 -ing 可表示正在閃爍，也可作形容詞表示「耀眼的」。glittering résumé 還可比喻「極其亮眼的履歷」。

exampleSentences.en: Yesterday, a government official visited the flooded neighborhood and spoke with residents.
exampleSentences.zh: 昨天，一名政府官員走訪淹水社區並與居民交談。

exampleSentences.en: Every government official involved in procurement must disclose potential conflicts of interest.
exampleSentences.zh: 每位參與採購的政府官員都必須揭露潛在的利益衝突。

government official.mnemonicHint: government 修飾 official，整體是名詞片語「政府官員」，不是形容詞。official 單獨可指官員，也可作「官方的」；看到 a government official 時，中心詞是可數名詞 official。

exampleSentences.en: After finding her lost wallet, Nora sent the bus driver a note of gratitude.
exampleSentences.zh: 找回遺失的錢包後，諾拉寄了一張感謝卡給公車司機。

exampleSentences.en: Public expressions of gratitude can strengthen cooperation by assuring contributors that their efforts are valued.
exampleSentences.zh: 公開表達感謝能讓貢獻者確信其付出受到重視，進而強化合作。

gratitude.mnemonicHint: gratitude 和 grateful 都帶 grat-，可聯想到「感激」。常見搭配是 express/show gratitude to someone 或 gratitude for something，表示對人或事的謝意。

exampleSentences.en: Our tenant filed a grievance after the landlord ignored three requests to repair the heater.
exampleSentences.zh: 房東無視三次修理暖氣的要求後，我們的房客提出了申訴。

exampleSentences.en: Workers may submit a formal grievance when they believe the promotion process violates company policy.
exampleSentences.zh: 員工若認為升遷程序違反公司政策，可以提出正式申訴。

grievance.mnemonicHint: grievance 與 grieve「悲痛」同源，可想成一件讓人難受、一直放在心上的不公平，因此成為「不滿」或正式「申訴」。常見搭配：file/air a grievance。

have stuck.chinese: 已黏住；已卡住；已堅持（stick 的現在完成式形式）

exampleSentences.en: Several wet leaves have stuck to the kitchen window overnight.
exampleSentences.zh: 幾片濕葉子一夜之間黏在了廚房窗戶上。

exampleSentences.en: Although rival firms abandoned the standard, several manufacturers have stuck with it to preserve compatibility.
exampleSentences.zh: 儘管競爭公司放棄了該標準，數家製造商仍堅持採用，以維持相容性。

have stuck.mnemonicHint: stick 的過去式與過去分詞都是 stuck，所以 have stuck 是正確的現在完成式，不是 malformed form。實物 have stuck to 表示「已黏上」；人 have stuck with 表示「一直堅持」。

exampleSentences.en: Having affected the coastal villages, the typhoon moved north before dawn.
exampleSentences.zh: 颱風影響沿海村落後，在黎明前向北移動。

exampleSentences.en: Researchers, having affected local water quality through the trial, were required to fund restoration work.
exampleSentences.zh: 研究人員因試驗已影響當地水質，被要求出資進行復原工作。

having affected.mnemonicHint: 這不是單字而是 having + affected：having 表示前一動作已完成，affected 是 affect（影響）的過去分詞；看到 having affected X，就理解為「在已經影響 X 之後」。正式詞條應回歸 affect 或 affected，並注意 effect 作動詞是「促成、實現」，意思不同。

hedgehog.chinese: 刺蝟；（比喻）只憑一個核心觀念思考的人

exampleSentences.en: At dusk, a hedgehog shuffled under the garden gate in search of beetles.
exampleSentences.zh: 黃昏時，一隻刺蝟慢慢鑽過花園門，尋找甲蟲。

exampleSentences.en: Unlike a fox, the hedgehog in Berlin's famous metaphor interprets the world through one central idea.
exampleSentences.zh: 在柏林著名的比喻中，刺蝟不同於狐狸，會透過一個核心觀念解讀世界。

hedgehog.mnemonicHint: hedge（樹籬）+ hog（豬）：想像一隻像小豬的刺球躲在樹籬下，就是 hedgehog。比喻義來自「刺蝟只知道一件大事」，因此可指緊守單一核心想法的人；動物上的 porcupine 是豪豬，不是刺蝟。

exampleSentences.en: This curved hook is perfect for hooking the fallen branch and pulling it ashore.
exampleSentences.zh: 這個彎鉤很適合鉤住落下的樹枝，再把它拉到岸邊。

exampleSentences.en: By highlighting the human cost of inflation, the opening paragraph succeeds in hooking the reader's attention.
exampleSentences.zh: 開頭段落凸顯通膨的人力代價，成功抓住讀者的注意力。

hooking.mnemonicHint: hook 是「鉤子」，加 -ing 就是正在用鉤子勾住；抽象用法也像鉤子抓牢注意力。記住具體畫面「魚鉤 hooking 住魚」，就能延伸到 hooking an audience（吸引觀眾）。

hopping.chinese: 單腳跳；蹦跳；快速換乘或移動

exampleSentences.en: After hopping over three puddles, Mina noticed mud on both shoes.
exampleSentences.zh: 米娜跳過三個水窪後，發現兩隻鞋都沾了泥。

exampleSentences.en: Because electrons can move by hopping between localized states, conductivity rises as temperature increases.
exampleSentences.zh: 由於電子能在局域態之間躍遷，導電率會隨溫度升高而上升。

hopping.mnemonicHint: hop 是短促的一跳，重複尾字母 p 再加 -ing 成 hopping；想像兔子 hop、hop、hop 地連跳。不要寫成 hoping：hop 要雙寫 p，hope 則去 e 加 -ing。

exampleSentences.en: Once a quiet warehouse district, the neighborhood is now a hotbed of live music.
exampleSentences.zh: 這個社區曾是安靜的倉庫區，如今已成為現場音樂的熱門據點。

exampleSentences.en: During periods of weak oversight, anonymous forums may become a hotbed of coordinated misinformation.
exampleSentences.zh: 在監管薄弱的時期，匿名論壇可能成為協同散播錯誤資訊的溫床。

hotbed.mnemonicHint: hot + bed 原指用發酵肥料加熱、催苗的「熱苗床」，後來比喻讓活動快速滋長的「溫床」。它是可數名詞，常見句型為 a hotbed of + 活動／問題；manifest 的 v/adj 詞性應更正為 n。

hushing.chinese: 使安靜；壓低聲音；壓制消息或異議

exampleSentences.en: Please stop hushing the children; they are only cheering for their team.
exampleSentences.zh: 請別再叫孩子們安靜；他們只是在替自己的隊伍加油。

exampleSentences.en: By hushing dissenting voices, the committee concealed weaknesses in the proposed policy.
exampleSentences.zh: 委員會藉由壓制異議，掩蓋了擬議政策的弱點。

hushing.mnemonicHint: hush! 是叫人「噓、安靜」，加 -ing 變成 hushing，表示正在讓聲音或意見沉下去。想像有人把食指放在嘴前說 hush；別和 husking（剝外殼）混淆，後者多一個 k。

husking.chinese: 剝去穀物、玉米等的外殼或苞葉

exampleSentences.en: Before husking the corn, Leo spread an old sheet across the kitchen floor.
exampleSentences.zh: 剝玉米苞葉前，里歐先在廚房地板鋪了一張舊床單。

exampleSentences.en: Using motorized rollers for husking rice reduced processing time but damaged some grains.
exampleSentences.zh: 使用機動滾輪替稻米脫殼雖縮短了加工時間，卻也損傷了部分米粒。

husking.mnemonicHint: husk 是種子或玉米的外殼，husking 就是把這層外衣剝掉。把 k 想成一把尖工具插進 husk：有 k 才是在剝殼；沒有 k 的 hushing 則是在叫人安靜。

impassive.chinese: 無動於衷的；面無表情的

exampleSentences.en: Even when the alarm sounded, the guard's face remained impassive.
exampleSentences.zh: 即使警報響起，警衛仍然面無表情。

exampleSentences.en: Although the witness remained impassive during questioning, changes in her pulse suggested considerable stress.
exampleSentences.zh: 雖然證人在訊問時始終面無表情，她的脈搏變化卻顯示出相當大的壓力。

impassive.mnemonicHint: im-（不）+ passive（感受、反應的）可聯想成「不把情緒傳出來」，所以 impassive 是面無表情。特別小心 impassioned 是「充滿激情的」，幾乎相反；impassable 則是「無法通行的」。

exampleSentences.en: With an imperious wave, the customer ordered the waiter to bring another chair.
exampleSentences.zh: 那名顧客專橫地揮了揮手，命令服務生再拿一把椅子來。

exampleSentences.en: Leaders who adopt an imperious tone may secure immediate obedience while weakening long-term trust.
exampleSentences.zh: 領導者若採取專橫的語氣，或許能立即得到服從，卻會削弱長期信任。

imperious.mnemonicHint: imper- 來自拉丁文 imperium（統治、命令權），所以 imperious 像掌權者用不容反駁的口氣下令。imperial 偏「帝國的」，imperious 則描述人的態度「專橫的」。

inclusive.chinese: 包容的；涵蓋廣泛的；包括在內的

exampleSentences.en: Our neighborhood festival welcomes every family and offers inclusive activities for all ages.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們的社區節慶歡迎每個家庭參加，並提供各年齡層都能參與的包容性活動。

exampleSentences.en: To create an inclusive workplace, employers must remove barriers rather than merely invite diverse applicants.
exampleSentences.zh: 為了打造包容的職場，雇主必須消除障礙，而不只是邀請多元背景的求職者。

inclusive.mnemonicHint: in-（進入）+ clus（關閉、圈住）+ -ive：把每個人都圈「進」共同範圍，就是 inclusive。句法上 inclusive 是形容詞；including 是介系詞／分詞「包括……」，不能因為句子需要 including 就用 inclusive 代替。

indict.chinese: 起訴；正式控告（刑事罪行）

exampleSentences.en: Local prosecutors may indict the driver after reviewing the traffic-camera footage.
exampleSentences.zh: 地方檢察官查看行車監視器畫面後，可能會起訴那名駕駛。

exampleSentences.en: A grand jury declined to indict the executive because the evidence did not establish criminal intent.
exampleSentences.zh: 大陪審團拒絕起訴該名主管，因為證據不足以證明其犯罪意圖。

indict.mnemonicHint: indict 的 c 不發音，讀作 in-DITE；把它想成檢察官把罪名寫進（in）正式起訴書，表示「正式起訴」，而不是已經判決有罪（convict）。

exampleSentences.en: Our neighborhood clinic reduces health inequality by offering free weekend screenings.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們社區的診所透過提供免費週末篩檢來縮小健康不平等。

exampleSentences.en: Persistent income inequality can limit social mobility even when access to primary education is universal.
exampleSentences.zh: 即使初等教育已全面普及，持續存在的所得不平等仍可能限制社會流動。

inequality.mnemonicHint: in-（不）＋ equality（平等）就是「不平等」；看到 income、gender、health 等名詞接在前面時，通常是在談某領域中可衡量的資源或機會差距。

ingenuous.chinese: 坦率天真的；單純而毫無心機的

exampleSentences.en: Her ingenuous question about salaries made the experienced managers exchange awkward glances.
exampleSentences.zh: 她天真坦率地詢問薪資，讓資深經理們尷尬地互看了一眼。

exampleSentences.en: The witness appeared ingenuous, but the court still required independent evidence to verify his account.
exampleSentences.zh: 那名證人看來坦率單純，但法院仍要求獨立證據來核實他的陳述。

ingenuous.mnemonicHint: ingenuous 形容人「天真坦率、沒有心機」；別和 ingenious（有巧思的、聰明的）混淆。記成 genuine 前面多一個 in：內心 genuine，所以說話毫無算計。

inheriting.chinese: 正在繼承；承接（特質、問題或制度）

exampleSentences.en: After inheriting her aunt's bakery, Mei kept the original sourdough recipe.
exampleSentences.zh: 美繼承姑媽的麵包店後，保留了原本的酸種麵包配方。

exampleSentences.en: By inheriting outdated infrastructure, the new administration also assumed substantial maintenance costs.
exampleSentences.zh: 新政府承接老舊基礎設施的同時，也承擔了龐大的維護成本。

inheriting.mnemonicHint: inherit 是「繼承」，-ing 表示動作正在進行或作為分詞使用；可繼承的不只遺產，也能承接基因、傳統、債務與前任留下的問題。

exampleSentences.en: Despite the accusation, Lena maintained her innocence and showed the receipt from that evening.
exampleSentences.zh: 儘管受到指控，莉娜仍堅稱自己清白，並出示了當晚的收據。

exampleSentences.en: DNA evidence established the prisoner's innocence after he had spent twelve years in custody.
exampleSentences.zh: DNA 證據證實該名囚犯無罪，而他此前已被關押十二年。

innocence.mnemonicHint: innocence 是 innocent 的名詞：in-（不）＋ noc（傷害、罪害）可聯想成「沒有造成罪害」，因此既可指法律上的清白，也可指孩子般的天真無邪。

insighted.chinese: 非標準形式；意指有洞察力的

exampleSentences.en: During proofreading, Ana replaced the nonstandard word 'insighted' with 'insightful' in her review.
exampleSentences.zh: 校稿時，安娜把評論中不合標準的 insighted 改成了 insightful。

exampleSentences.en: Although 'insighted' occasionally appears in informal writing, academic editors normally require the standard adjective 'insightful.'
exampleSentences.zh: 雖然 insighted 偶爾出現在非正式寫作中，學術編輯通常仍要求使用標準形容詞 insightful。

insighted.mnemonicHint: insighted 是把 insight 誤加 -ed 形成的非標準形式；要說「有洞察力的」應用 insight＋ful＝insightful。把 -ful 記成「充滿洞見」，就不會誤寫成 -ed。

installed.chinese: 已安裝的；裝設了；使就任了

exampleSentences.en: Yesterday the technician installed a quieter fan in my laptop.
exampleSentences.zh: 技師昨天在我的筆電裡裝了一個更安靜的風扇。

exampleSentences.en: Engineers installed vibration sensors along the bridge to detect structural damage before it became visible.
exampleSentences.zh: 工程師沿著橋梁裝設振動感測器，以便在結構損傷肉眼可見之前偵測到它。

installed.mnemonicHint: install＝in（放進）＋ stall（固定位置）可聯想成「放進定位並完成裝設」；installed 是其過去式或過去分詞，別和 instilled（逐步灌輸）混淆。

instigated.chinese: 煽動了；挑起了；促使（事件）發生

exampleSentences.en: One false rumor instigated an argument between two previously friendly neighbors.
exampleSentences.zh: 一則不實謠言挑起了兩名原本友善的鄰居之間的爭吵。

exampleSentences.en: Officials concluded that the sudden tax increase had instigated the nationwide protests.
exampleSentences.zh: 官員認定，突然加稅引發了全國性的抗議。

instigated.mnemonicHint: instigate 常帶負面意味，表示「煽動、挑起」衝突或事件；可聯想 agitator（煽動者）在群眾中推動事態。instigated 是已經把事情挑起來了。

instilled.chinese: 逐步灌輸了；使逐漸形成（觀念或感受）

exampleSentences.en: Weekly cooking lessons instilled confidence in Ravi, who had once feared using the stove.
exampleSentences.zh: 每週的烹飪課逐漸讓拉維建立信心；他以前連使用爐子都害怕。

exampleSentences.en: The academy's mentoring program instilled a strong sense of public duty in its graduates.
exampleSentences.zh: 該學院的導師制度在畢業生心中逐步培養出強烈的公共責任感。

instilled.mnemonicHint: instill 原意像「一滴一滴注入」，所以不是一次塞入資訊，而是長時間把信心、價值觀或習慣慢慢灌輸進心裡；installed 則是安裝實體設備。

integrates.chinese: 整合；使融入；結合成完整體（第三人稱單數）

exampleSentences.en: This calendar app integrates my work shifts with my family's appointments.
exampleSentences.zh: 這款行事曆應用程式把我的工作班表與家人的約會整合在一起。

exampleSentences.en: The proposed framework integrates economic, ecological, and cultural evidence into a single account of coastal change.
exampleSentences.zh: 該框架把經濟、生態與文化證據整合成對海岸變遷的單一解釋。

integrates.mnemonicHint: integrate 和 integer（整數、完整體）同源；integrates 就是主詞把多個部分「整合成一個完整體」，字尾 -s 表示現在式第三人稱單數。

intelligence.chinese: 智力；理解與解決問題的能力；情報

exampleSentences.en: Her quick intelligence helped us repair the leaking faucet without calling a plumber.
exampleSentences.zh: 她的敏捷才智讓我們不用叫水電工就修好了漏水的水龍頭。

exampleSentences.en: Modern intelligence-gathering systems can identify unusual activity patterns, but human analysts must still interpret their significance.
exampleSentences.zh: 現代情報蒐集系統能辨識異常活動模式，但仍須由人類分析師解讀其意義。

intelligence.mnemonicHint: intelligence 裡有 intelligent（聰明的）：想像情報員不只蒐集 information，還要靠 intelligence 理解線索、作出判斷，因此可同時記住「智力」與「情報」兩義。

exampleSentences.en: Dark clouds began to intensify the chill as we walked home.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們走回家時，烏雲開始加重寒意。

exampleSentences.en: Rising sea temperatures may intensify tropical storms by supplying them with additional energy.
exampleSentences.zh: 海水溫度上升可能提供更多能量，進而加劇熱帶風暴。

intensify.mnemonicHint: intense（強烈的）＋ -ify（使成為）＝使某事變得更 intense，所以 intensify 就是「使加強、使加劇」。

exampleSentences.en: My younger sister is interested in astronomy and watches the moon through a small telescope.
exampleSentences.zh: 我妹妹對天文學感興趣，會用小型望遠鏡觀察月亮。

exampleSentences.en: Researchers interested in urban migration examined housing records from three rapidly growing cities.
exampleSentences.zh: 對都市遷移感興趣的研究人員檢視了三座快速成長城市的住宅紀錄。

interested in.mnemonicHint: 人當主語時用 interested in：I am interested in robots，表示「我心裡對機器人有興趣」；記住感受者用 -ed，興趣指向的對象接 in。

interesting to.chinese: 對……而言有趣；令……感興趣（後接感受者）

exampleSentences.en: That antique map is interesting to Leo because it marks a vanished railway.
exampleSentences.zh: 那張古地圖讓里歐覺得很有趣，因為上面標出了一條已消失的鐵路。

exampleSentences.en: Patterns that appear random to adults may be interesting to children who are testing simple rules.
exampleSentences.zh: 成人眼中看似隨機的圖樣，對正在測試簡單規則的兒童而言可能很有趣。

interesting to.mnemonicHint: 事物用 interesting，感受者放在 to 後面：The puzzle is interesting to me；和 I am interested in the puzzle 對照，就不會把 -ing 與 -ed 搞反。

is considered.chinese: 被認為；被視為（常接名詞、形容詞或 to be）

exampleSentences.en: This chipped mug is considered lucky in our family, so nobody throws it away.
exampleSentences.zh: 這個有缺口的杯子在我們家被視為幸運物，所以沒有人把它丟掉。

exampleSentences.en: A species is considered endangered when evidence indicates a high risk of extinction in the wild.
exampleSentences.zh: 當證據顯示某物種在野外有很高的滅絕風險時，它便被視為瀕危物種。

is considered.mnemonicHint: consider 是「考慮、認為」，加上 is 與過去分詞 considered 形成被動：is considered＝「經過考量後被認為」；若補身分，常用 is considered a genius 或 is considered to be safe。

is regarded.chinese: 被認為；被視為（通常接 as）

exampleSentences.en: Around our neighborhood, Ms. Chen is regarded as the best person to ask about roses.
exampleSentences.zh: 在我們社區，陳女士被公認是最適合請教玫瑰種植的人。

exampleSentences.en: Within classical economics, voluntary exchange is regarded as mutually beneficial when both parties possess adequate information.
exampleSentences.zh: 在古典經濟學中，若雙方都掌握充分資訊，自願交換會被視為互利。

is regarded.mnemonicHint: regard 可聯想「朝某方向看」；is regarded as 就是「被大家以某種眼光看作……」。記住 regard 後面的身分標籤通常由 as 引出。

exampleSentences.en: On this worksheet, "is seemed" is incorrect; write "seems" in "The door seems stuck."
exampleSentences.zh: 在這張學習單上，is seemed 是錯誤形式；「門似乎卡住了」應寫成 The door seems stuck。

exampleSentences.en: Because seem is normally intransitive, "is seemed" is ungrammatical here and should be corrected to "seemed" in the past-tense sentence.
exampleSentences.zh: 因為 seem 通常是不及物動詞，此處的 is seemed 不合文法；在過去式句子中應改為 seemed。

is seemed.mnemonicHint: 把 seem 記成自己就能變化的連綴動詞：seems／seemed，不需要 be 幫忙組被動。因此看到 is seemed 要亮紅燈；若想表達「被看見」，那是 is seen。

is viewed.chinese: 被看待；被視為（常接 as）

exampleSentences.en: In my grandparents' eyes, repairing old furniture is viewed as a satisfying weekend project.
exampleSentences.zh: 在我祖父母眼中，修理舊家具被視為一項令人滿足的週末活動。

exampleSentences.en: Across many legal systems, judicial independence is viewed as essential to protecting citizens from arbitrary power.
exampleSentences.zh: 在許多法律體系中，司法獨立被視為保護公民免受恣意權力侵害的必要條件。

is viewed.mnemonicHint: view 是「觀看、觀點」；is viewed as 就像某事物「被放進某個觀點框裡」，因此表示「被看作……」。別和多一個 re- 的 is reviewed（被審查）混淆。

jeopardy.chinese: 危險；危難（常用 in jeopardy）

exampleSentences.en: Leaving the freezer open put all our food in jeopardy during the power outage.
exampleSentences.zh: 停電時讓冷凍庫敞開，使我們所有的食物都面臨損壞的危險。

exampleSentences.en: Without immediate habitat protection, the survival of the island's nesting seabirds remains in jeopardy.
exampleSentences.zh: 若不立即保護棲地，島上築巢海鳥的生存仍將岌岌可危。

jeopardy.mnemonicHint: 把 jeopardy 想成競賽節目答錯後獎金「陷入危險」；固定搭配 in jeopardy＝處於危險中，而動詞 jeopardize 則是「使……陷入危險」。

jovial.chinese: 快活友善的；興高采烈的

exampleSentences.en: Despite the long queue, the jovial baker joked with every customer and handed children warm rolls.
exampleSentences.zh: 儘管排隊人龍很長，那位快活的麵包師仍和每位顧客開玩笑，還遞給孩子們熱麵包。

exampleSentences.en: Rather than sounding hostile, the speaker adopted a jovial tone that eased tension during the negotiations.
exampleSentences.zh: 講者沒有以敵意口吻發言，而是採取快活友善的語調，緩和了談判中的緊張氣氛。

jovial.mnemonicHint: jovial 源自 Jove（朱庇特）；想像眾神之王在宴會上豪爽大笑、讓全場氣氛歡樂，就能記住 jovial 是「快活而友善的」。

lampoons.chinese: 諷刺作品；嘲諷文章（lampoon 的複數）

exampleSentences.en: Those sharp lampoons made everyone at the comedy club laugh.
exampleSentences.zh: 那些尖銳的諷刺作品逗得喜劇俱樂部裡的每個人都笑了。

exampleSentences.en: Political lampoons can expose abuses of power through exaggeration and ridicule.
exampleSentences.zh: 政治諷刺作品能透過誇張與嘲弄揭露權力濫用。

lampoons.mnemonicHint: 把 lampoons 想成用文字當『砲』轟名人：lampoon 是一篇嘲諷作品，加 -s 就是多篇諷刺作品。

exampleSentences.en: After the heavy lunch, a pleasant languor settled over me.
exampleSentences.zh: 吃完豐盛的午餐後，一股愜意的倦怠感籠罩著我。

exampleSentences.en: Prolonged heat produced such languor among the workers that afternoon output declined.
exampleSentences.zh: 持續的高溫使工人們倦怠不振，導致午後產量下降。

languor.mnemonicHint: languor 和 languish（衰弱）同源；想像人在漫長午後懶洋洋地癱著，正是 languor 的倦怠狀態。

exampleSentences.en: One brief lapse in attention made me miss my train stop.
exampleSentences.zh: 一時分心讓我坐過了火車站。

exampleSentences.en: If the patent is allowed to lapse, competitors may legally use the invention.
exampleSentences.zh: 若專利任其失效，競爭者便可能合法使用該發明。

lapse.mnemonicHint: lapse 像注意力『落下去』的一瞬間，可指疏忽；資格或期限落空時，則表示失效。elapse 多半只指時間流逝。

exampleSentences.en: Police charged the shoplifter with petty larceny yesterday.
exampleSentences.zh: 警方昨天以輕微竊盜罪起訴那名商店竊賊。

exampleSentences.en: Unlike robbery, larceny does not necessarily involve force or intimidation.
exampleSentences.zh: 不同於搶劫，竊盜罪未必涉及武力或恐嚇。

larceny.mnemonicHint: 把 larceny 聯想成『拿了財（lar-ce-ny）卻沒告知』；法律上核心是未經同意取走他人財物，別和使用暴力的 robbery 混淆。

exampleSentences.en: Grandma fries the turnip cake in a spoonful of lard.
exampleSentences.zh: 奶奶用一匙豬油煎蘿蔔糕。

exampleSentences.en: Before vegetable shortening became widespread, bakers often used lard to produce flaky pastry.
exampleSentences.zh: 在植物性酥油普及以前，烘焙師常用豬油製作酥鬆的糕點。

lard.mnemonicHint: lard 就是從豬脂肪熬出的白色油脂；想像 larder（食品儲藏室）裡放著一罐 lard，但兩字不可混用。

large enough.chinese: 夠大；尺寸足以符合需求

exampleSentences.en: This suitcase is large enough to hold both winter coats.
exampleSentences.zh: 這個行李箱夠大，可以裝下兩件冬季外套。

exampleSentences.en: A sample large enough to represent the population reduces the risk of misleading conclusions.
exampleSentences.zh: 足以代表母體的大型樣本可降低得出誤導性結論的風險。

large enough.mnemonicHint: large 描述尺寸，enough 表示達標；large enough 的順序就是『尺寸大到足夠』，例如 a room large enough for fifty people。

largely enough.chinese: 非標準形式；夠大或大致足夠

exampleSentences.en: The phrase 'largely enough' sounds wrong here; say 'large enough' for a box of sufficient size.
exampleSentences.zh: 此處的 largely enough 不自然；要說箱子尺寸足夠，應改用 large enough。

exampleSentences.en: When an adjective describes sufficient size, 'largely enough' is malformed and should be corrected to 'large enough.'
exampleSentences.zh: 當形容詞描述尺寸足夠時，largely enough 是錯誤形式，應修正為 large enough。

largely enough.mnemonicHint: largely 是『主要地、大致上』的副詞，不等於『大的』；尺寸 + 足夠要用形容詞 large + enough，所以把多出的 -ly 劃掉：largely enough → large enough。

exampleSentences.en: Our neighborhood leveraged volunteer skills to repair the playground cheaply.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們的社區善用志工技能，以低成本修繕遊樂場。

exampleSentences.en: By leveraging its extensive distribution network, the firm entered rural markets ahead of its rivals.
exampleSentences.zh: 該公司善用廣泛的配銷網絡，搶在競爭對手之前進入鄉村市場。

leverage.mnemonicHint: leverage 來自 lever（槓桿）：用小力撬動大物；引申為善用既有資源，放大成果或取得影響力。

litigants.chinese: 訴訟當事人（litigant 的複數）

exampleSentences.en: Both litigants waited outside the courtroom with their lawyers.
exampleSentences.zh: 兩名訴訟當事人和各自的律師在法庭外等候。

exampleSentences.en: Because the litigants accepted mediation, the costly civil trial was avoided.
exampleSentences.zh: 由於訴訟雙方接受調解，因而避免了代價高昂的民事審判。

litigants.mnemonicHint: litigants 是進入 litigation（訴訟）的人；字尾 -ant 表示參與者，加 -s 表示原告、被告等多位訴訟當事人。

exampleSentences.en: Several local workshops manufacture custom bicycles by hand.
exampleSentences.zh: 幾家本地工坊以手工製造客製化自行車。

exampleSentences.en: Modern plants manufacture semiconductors in tightly controlled, dust-free environments.
exampleSentences.zh: 現代工廠在嚴格管控的無塵環境中製造半導體。

manufacture.mnemonicHint: manu- 是『手』，fact 是『做』：manufacture 原意是用手做，現代則多指工廠製造或大量生產。

measurable.chinese: 可測量的；可量化的；明顯到足以衡量的

exampleSentences.en: Regular walks made a measurable difference to my blood pressure.
exampleSentences.zh: 規律散步讓我的血壓出現了可測量的改善。

exampleSentences.en: The policy produced a measurable decline in household energy consumption.
exampleSentences.zh: 該政策使家庭能源消耗出現可量化的下降。

measurable.mnemonicHint: measure（測量）加上 -able（能夠……的），就是『能被測量的』；看到 measurable 就想像拿尺把成果的差距實際量出來。

exampleSentences.en: Despite the fancy decor, the restaurant served mediocre pasta.
exampleSentences.zh: 儘管裝潢華麗，那家餐廳的義大利麵卻很普通。

exampleSentences.en: A mediocre response may identify the problem without evaluating its broader consequences.
exampleSentences.zh: 平庸的作答或許能指出問題，卻不會評估其更廣泛的後果。

mediocre.mnemonicHint: mediocre 和 medium 都帶有『中間』的感覺：成績卡卡在中間，沒有糟到墊底，也完全稱不上出色，就是平庸。

exampleSentences.en: After waiting in wet shoes all afternoon, Leo felt miserable.
exampleSentences.zh: 穿著濕鞋等了一整個下午後，里歐覺得難受極了。

exampleSentences.en: Workers endured miserable conditions until the factory adopted basic safety standards.
exampleSentences.zh: 工人忍受著悲慘的環境，直到工廠採用基本安全標準。

miserable.mnemonicHint: 把 miserable 連到 misery（痛苦）：一個人被 misery 包住，冷、濕、累又無助，那種整體感受就是 miserable。

misfit.chinese: 不合群的人；與環境格格不入者

exampleSentences.en: At the formal dinner, Ben felt like a misfit in his hiking boots.
exampleSentences.zh: 在正式晚宴上，穿著登山靴的班覺得自己格格不入。

exampleSentences.en: Rather than dismissing the inventor as a misfit, the committee examined her unconventional proposal.
exampleSentences.zh: 委員會沒有把這位發明家視為怪人而不予理會，而是審視了她非傳統的提案。

misfit.mnemonicHint: mis-（錯、不合）加 fit（適合）：像一塊放錯位置、怎麼都嵌不進拼圖的拼片，因此指與群體或環境格格不入的人。

morbid.chinese: 病態的；對死亡或可怕事物過度著迷的

exampleSentences.en: Curiosity turned morbid when he began collecting photographs of fatal accidents.
exampleSentences.zh: 當他開始蒐集致命事故的照片時，那份好奇心變得病態。

exampleSentences.en: The novel's morbid imagery reflects a society preoccupied with disease and death.
exampleSentences.zh: 小說中病態陰森的意象，反映了一個沉迷於疾病與死亡的社會。

morbid.mnemonicHint: morbid 源自拉丁文 morbus（疾病）；想像注意力病態地黏在死亡與災難上，便能記住它不只是陰暗，而是『不健康地著迷』。

no meaning.chinese: 無意義（清單中的片語殘片；自然用法通常是 have/has no meaning）

exampleSentences.en: Without the map legend, these colored lines have no meaning to me.
exampleSentences.zh: 沒有地圖圖例，這些彩色線條對我毫無意義。

exampleSentences.en: A correlation has no meaning unless the variables and sampling method are clearly defined.
exampleSentences.zh: 除非變數與抽樣方法都有明確定義，否則相關性並無意義。

no meaning.mnemonicHint: 這不是完整的固定片語，而是 no（沒有）加 meaning（意義）的殘片；造句時前面補 have/has，形成 have no meaning，才是自然完整的表達。

no means.chinese: 絕非（清單漏掉 by；正確固定片語為 by no means）

exampleSentences.en: This repair is by no means cheap, but it should last for years.
exampleSentences.zh: 這次維修絕不便宜，但應該能維持多年。

exampleSentences.en: Economic growth is by no means sufficient to guarantee an equitable distribution of wealth.
exampleSentences.zh: 經濟成長絕不足以保證財富的公平分配。

no means.mnemonicHint: no means 單獨不是表示『絕非』的標準片語，前面一定要有 by：by no means 可想成『不靠任何方法都辦不到』，語氣就是『絕對不』。

not mean.chinese: 不表示；並非意指（清單中的未完整動詞片語，需搭配主詞或助動詞）

exampleSentences.en: Skipping dessert does not mean I dislike your cooking.
exampleSentences.zh: 不吃甜點並不表示我不喜歡你做的菜。

exampleSentences.en: The absence of evidence does not mean that the proposed mechanism is impossible.
exampleSentences.zh: 缺乏證據並不表示所提出的機制不可能存在。

not mean.mnemonicHint: not mean 只是『不＋表示』的骨架，不能孤零零當完整詞條；記成 does not mean 或 do not mean，並依主詞補上正確助動詞。

exampleSentences.en: Her quiet reply does not mean she is angry.
exampleSentences.zh: 她安靜的回答並不表示她在生氣。

exampleSentences.en: A temporary decline does not mean that the long-term trend has reversed.
exampleSentences.zh: 短期下降並不表示長期趨勢已經逆轉。

not means.mnemonicHint: not 後面的動詞要用原形，所以 not means 是錯的；把第三人稱單數的 -s 移到助動詞 does，得到 does not mean。

obscure.chinese: 模糊的；晦澀的；鮮為人知的；遮蔽

exampleSentences.en: Steam began to obscure the bathroom mirror.
exampleSentences.zh: 水蒸氣開始遮住浴室鏡面。

exampleSentences.en: Technical jargon can obscure the assumptions underlying an economic model.
exampleSentences.zh: 技術術語可能掩蓋經濟模型背後的假設。

obscure.mnemonicHint: ob- 有『朝向、覆在上面』的感覺，scure 可聯想被遮暗；像霧覆上玻璃，使東西看不清，也延伸成文字晦澀或事物鮮為人知。

offensive.chinese: 冒犯的；令人不快的；攻擊性的

exampleSentences.en: That crude joke was offensive to several guests at dinner.
exampleSentences.zh: 那個低俗笑話冒犯了晚餐會上的幾位客人。

exampleSentences.en: The survey found that offensive advertising can damage consumers' trust in a brand.
exampleSentences.zh: 該調查發現，冒犯性的廣告可能損害消費者對品牌的信任。

offensive.mnemonicHint: offend 是「冒犯」，加形容詞字尾 -ive 成為 offensive；也可聯想球賽的 offense 是主動進攻，因此既有「攻擊性的」也有「冒犯的」意思。

exampleSentences.en: Maya openly challenges the rule whenever it seems unfair.
exampleSentences.zh: 每當規則顯得不公平時，瑪雅就會公開質疑它。

exampleSentences.en: This finding openly challenges the assumption that economic growth always reduces inequality.
exampleSentences.zh: 這項發現公開挑戰了經濟成長必然降低不平等的假設。

openly challenges.mnemonicHint: openly 是「公開地」，challenges 是 challenge 遇到第三人稱單數主詞的形式；合起來就是某人不躲藏地把質疑擺上檯面。

opposable.chinese: 可反對的；可對置的（尤指拇指能與其他手指相對）

exampleSentences.en: An opposable thumb lets you grip a slippery jar securely.
exampleSentences.zh: 可與其他手指相對的拇指讓你能牢牢抓住濕滑的罐子。

exampleSentences.en: Primates use opposable digits to manipulate objects with remarkable precision.
exampleSentences.zh: 靈長類利用可對置的指頭，以驚人的精準度操控物體。

opposable.mnemonicHint: oppose（使相對、反對）加 -able（能夠）就是「能夠相對或被反對的」；想像拇指轉過來與食指面對面夾住硬幣。

outcast.chinese: 被排斥者；遭放逐的人；被排斥的

exampleSentences.en: After exposing the lie, Leo felt like an outcast among his former friends.
exampleSentences.zh: 揭穿謊言後，里歐覺得自己在昔日朋友之間像個被排斥的人。

exampleSentences.en: The novel portrays its protagonist as a social outcast who questions established customs.
exampleSentences.zh: 這部小說將主角描寫成一名質疑既定習俗的社會邊緣人。

outcast.mnemonicHint: out（出去）加 cast（丟、投）就是「被丟到群體外面的人」；把一個人從圈內 cast out，便成了 outcast。

outrageous.chinese: 令人憤慨的；駭人聽聞的；極端離譜的

exampleSentences.en: Charging fifty dollars for tap water is outrageous.
exampleSentences.zh: 一杯自來水收五十美元實在太離譜了。

exampleSentences.en: Critics condemned the outrageous misuse of public funds during the reconstruction project.
exampleSentences.zh: 批評者譴責重建計畫期間駭人聽聞的公款濫用行為。

outrageous.mnemonicHint: outrage 是強烈憤怒，加 -ous 變成「會引發強烈憤怒的」；價格或行為誇張到讓人喊出 outrage，就是 outrageous。

exampleSentences.en: We phased the apartment repairs over three weekends to control costs.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們把公寓修繕分三個週末進行，以控制成本。

exampleSentences.en: The ministry phased its reforms carefully, while obsolete subsidies were phased out over five years.
exampleSentences.zh: 該部會謹慎地分階段推行改革，同時在五年內逐步淘汰過時的補貼。

phased.mnemonicHint: phase 是「階段」，phased 表示事情已被切成階段執行；別和 fazed（使慌亂）混淆，而 phased out 才是「逐步淘汰」。

phased out.chinese: 逐步淘汰；分階段停止使用

exampleSentences.en: Our office phased out paper receipts after adopting a digital system.
exampleSentences.zh: 辦公室採用數位系統後，逐步停止使用紙本收據。

exampleSentences.en: Several nations phased out leaded gasoline because of its severe effects on public health.
exampleSentences.zh: 數個國家因含鉛汽油嚴重危害公共健康而逐步將其淘汰。

phased out.mnemonicHint: phase 是「階段」，out 是「退出」；讓舊制度一個階段接一個階段退出舞台，就是 phased out。

pleasurable.chinese: 令人愉快的；帶來樂趣的

exampleSentences.en: Warm sunlight made the quiet walk especially pleasurable.
exampleSentences.zh: 溫暖的陽光讓這趟寧靜的散步格外愉快。

exampleSentences.en: Designers often combine useful feedback with pleasurable interaction to sustain user engagement.
exampleSentences.zh: 設計師常把實用回饋與愉悅互動結合，以維持使用者的投入。

pleasurable.mnemonicHint: pleasure（樂趣）加 -able（能帶來）形成 pleasurable，表示某個活動或感受「能帶來樂趣」；主詞通常是令人愉快的事物。

predestined.chinese: 命中注定的；預先注定的

exampleSentences.en: Nothing about her career was predestined; she changed direction twice.
exampleSentences.zh: 她的職涯沒有任何事情是命中注定的；她曾兩度改變方向。

exampleSentences.en: The doctrine suggests that certain outcomes are predestined rather than shaped by individual choice.
exampleSentences.zh: 該教義主張，某些結果是預先注定的，而非由個人選擇塑造。

predestined.mnemonicHint: pre- 是「事先」，destine 是「注定」；在事件發生前就已被命運寫好目的地，便是 predestined。

preempted.chinese: 搶先阻止；先發制人地取代

exampleSentences.en: Breaking news preempted my favorite program last night.
exampleSentences.zh: 昨晚突發新聞取代了我最喜歡的節目。

exampleSentences.en: Early diplomatic action preempted a conflict that might otherwise have destabilized the region.
exampleSentences.zh: 及早的外交行動搶先阻止了一場原本可能動搖該區域的衝突。

preempted.mnemonicHint: pre- 是「在前」，empt 源自「取得、買下」；先一步把位置或機會占走，就能搶先阻止、取代或中止後面的事。

exampleSentences.en: Canceling the picnic now would be premature because tomorrow's forecast may improve.
exampleSentences.zh: 現在就取消野餐還太早，因為明天的天氣預報可能會好轉。

exampleSentences.en: Drawing firm conclusions from such a small sample is scientifically premature.
exampleSentences.zh: 從如此小的樣本得出確定結論，在科學上言之過早。

premature.mnemonicHint: pre- 是「在前」，mature 是「成熟」；在成熟之前就發生，因此是「過早的、早產的」。

preoccupied.chinese: 全神貫注的；心事重重的（preoccupy 的過去式／過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: Maya seemed preoccupied with her interview and forgot to eat lunch.
exampleSentences.zh: 瑪雅滿腦子都是面試，甚至忘了吃午餐。

exampleSentences.en: Researchers preoccupied with confirming their hypothesis may overlook contradictory evidence.
exampleSentences.zh: 一心只想證實假說的研究者可能會忽略相矛盾的證據。

preoccupied.mnemonicHint: pre-（事先）＋occupy（占據）：某件事先占滿了腦袋，所以會「全神貫注」或「心事重重」。

exampleSentences.en: After examining my ankle, the doctor prescribed an anti-inflammatory drug.
exampleSentences.zh: 醫師檢查我的腳踝後，開了一種消炎藥。

exampleSentences.en: National regulations prescribe strict procedures for disposing of hazardous laboratory waste.
exampleSentences.zh: 國家法規對危險實驗室廢棄物的處置訂有嚴格程序。

prescribe.mnemonicHint: pre-（預先）＋scribe（寫）：醫師預先把用藥寫下來是「開藥」，制度預先寫明則是「規定」。

presidents.chinese: 總統；會長；董事長（president 的複數）

exampleSentences.en: Three former club presidents attended the anniversary dinner on Saturday.
exampleSentences.zh: 三位前社團會長星期六出席了週年晚宴。

exampleSentences.en: Successive presidents expanded the treaty while preserving its central security commitments.
exampleSentences.zh: 歷任總統在維持條約核心安全承諾的同時，擴大了條約範圍。

presidents.mnemonicHint: preside 是「主持」，加 -nt 成為主持的人 president，再加 -s 就是多位「總統、會長或董事長」；別看成 precedents（先例）。

profanities.chinese: 褻瀆語；髒話（profanity 的複數）

exampleSentences.en: Angry fans shouted profanities after the referee ended the match.
exampleSentences.zh: 裁判結束比賽後，憤怒的球迷高喊髒話。

exampleSentences.en: Repeated profanities in public broadcasts prompted regulators to review existing decency standards.
exampleSentences.zh: 公共廣播中反覆出現的髒話，促使監管機關檢討現行的適當言語標準。

profanities.mnemonicHint: profane 指「褻瀆的、不敬的」，名詞 profanity 是一句髒話或褻瀆語；字尾變 -ies 表示複數 profanities。

prompted.chinese: 促使；提示（prompt 的過去式／過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: A calendar alert prompted Leo to call his grandmother before dinner.
exampleSentences.zh: 行事曆提醒促使里奧在晚餐前打電話給祖母。

exampleSentences.en: Unexpected declines in bee populations prompted scientists to investigate pesticide exposure.
exampleSentences.zh: 蜜蜂數量意外下降，促使科學家調查農藥暴露問題。

prompted.mnemonicHint: prompt 原本可指舞台旁的「提詞」，有人一提示就促成下一個動作；prompted 是已經「提示了、促使了」。

exampleSentences.en: Teasing that nervous dog could provoke it into biting you.
exampleSentences.zh: 逗弄那隻緊張的狗可能會激怒牠，讓牠咬你。

exampleSentences.en: Sharp increases in food prices can provoke widespread social unrest.
exampleSentences.zh: 食品價格急遽上漲可能引發廣泛的社會動盪。

provoke.mnemonicHint: pro-（向前）＋voke（呼喊，見 voice）：向前大喊把反應叫出來，就是「挑釁、激怒或引發」。

quotient.chinese: 商數；（某種能力或特質的）指數

exampleSentences.en: Dividing twelve by three gives a quotient of four.
exampleSentences.zh: 十二除以三所得的商是四。

exampleSentences.en: An intelligence quotient measures selected cognitive abilities but cannot capture every form of intelligence.
exampleSentences.zh: 智商衡量特定的認知能力，卻無法涵蓋每一種智能。

quotient.mnemonicHint: quotient 和 quota 都有「分出一份」的概念：除法把總數分開後得到的結果就是「商」；清單標成 adj 並不正確，本字是名詞。

rampant.chinese: 猖獗的；氾濫的；失控蔓延的

exampleSentences.en: Mosquitoes grow rampant near the pond whenever summer rain leaves standing water.
exampleSentences.zh: 每逢夏雨留下積水，池塘附近的蚊子就會大量滋生。

exampleSentences.en: Without independent oversight, rampant corruption can erode public trust in government institutions.
exampleSentences.zh: 若缺乏獨立監督，猖獗的貪腐會侵蝕民眾對政府機構的信任。

rampant.mnemonicHint: 想像野草衝上 ramp（斜坡）後到處亂竄、無人能擋，便是 rampant：「猖獗且失控蔓延的」。

exampleSentences.en: During morning recess, the children traded stickers beside the playground.
exampleSentences.zh: 上午課間休息時，孩子們在遊樂場旁交換貼紙。

exampleSentences.en: Parliament entered a month-long recess before debate on the revised budget resumed.
exampleSentences.zh: 國會休會一個月，之後才恢復修訂預算案的辯論。

recess.mnemonicHint: re-（向後）＋cess（走，如 recede）：大家往後退、暫時離場就是「休會、休息」；牆面往後退則形成「凹處」。

redundancy.chinese: 冗餘；備援；（英）職位裁撤或被裁狀態

exampleSentences.en: The merger put several office workers at risk of redundancy.
exampleSentences.zh: 這次合併使數名辦公室員工面臨職位遭裁撤的風險。

exampleSentences.en: Organizational redundancy can protect critical operations from a single point of failure.
exampleSentences.zh: 組織中的備援配置可保護關鍵作業，避免單點故障造成中斷。

redundancy.mnemonicHint: re-（再次）＋und（像 one，一個）＋-ancy：同一功能再多放一個，就是「重複配置」；多到不需要時便成了「冗餘」。

regard of.chinese: 非標準形式；應改為 with regard to（關於）

exampleSentences.en: With regard to Friday's dinner, please tell me about any food allergies.
exampleSentences.zh: 關於星期五的晚餐，請告訴我你是否對任何食物過敏。

exampleSentences.en: With regard to long-term costs, the policy may still improve public health overall.
exampleSentences.zh: 就長期成本而言，這項政策整體上仍可能改善公共健康。

regard of.mnemonicHint: regard of 少了完整搭配；表達「關於」時固定使用 with regard to。regardless of 是另一個表示「不論」的片語，不要混為一談。

exampleSentences.en: I regret missing your call last night.
exampleSentences.zh: 我很後悔昨晚漏接了你的電話。

exampleSentences.en: Many firms later regretted cutting research budgets during the recession.
exampleSentences.zh: 許多公司後來後悔在經濟衰退期間削減研究預算。

regret.mnemonicHint: 把 regret 想成 re-（回頭）＋gret（聽起來像「great」）：回頭看才發現本可做得更好，心裡便感到「後悔」。

relapsed.chinese: 復發；故態復萌（relapse 的過去式／過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: After three smoke-free months, Leo relapsed during a stressful week.
exampleSentences.zh: 戒菸三個月後，里歐在壓力沉重的一週裡又復吸了。

exampleSentences.en: The patient relapsed when the treatment was discontinued prematurely.
exampleSentences.zh: 治療過早停止後，患者的病情復發了。

relapsed.mnemonicHint: re-（再次）＋lapse（滑落、失誤）：好轉後又「再次滑落」回原本的疾病或習慣，就是 relapsed。

relaxed.chinese: 放鬆的；寬鬆的；使放鬆（relax 的過去式／過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: A warm shower relaxed my sore shoulders.
exampleSentences.zh: 洗個熱水澡讓我痠痛的肩膀放鬆了。

exampleSentences.en: The central bank relaxed lending restrictions to stimulate investment.
exampleSentences.zh: 中央銀行放寬貸款限制，以刺激投資。

relaxed.mnemonicHint: re-（往回）＋lax（鬆的）：讓緊繃狀態回到鬆弛，身體是「放鬆」，規定則是「放寬」。

relayed.chinese: 轉達；轉送；接力傳遞（relay 的過去式／過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: Mina relayed the gate change to everyone in our group.
exampleSentences.zh: 米娜把登機門變更的消息轉告給我們群組裡的每個人。

exampleSentences.en: Researchers relayed the findings to local officials before publishing the report.
exampleSentences.zh: 研究人員在發布報告前，先將研究結果轉達給地方官員。

relayed.mnemonicHint: relay race 是「接力賽」：訊息像接力棒一樣從一人交到另一人，relayed 就是已經「轉達／傳遞」。

relegated.chinese: 降級；貶至次要地位；委派（relegate 的過去式／過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: The coach relegated Dan to the bench after repeated mistakes.
exampleSentences.zh: 丹屢次犯錯後，教練把他降為板凳球員。

exampleSentences.en: Manual record-keeping was relegated to a minor role after the database was introduced.
exampleSentences.zh: 資料庫導入後，人工記錄被降至次要地位。

relegated.mnemonicHint: relegate 裡藏著 legate（使節、被派者）：把人「派到」較遠、較不重要的位置，便引申為「降級、貶至次要地位」。

exampleSentences.en: We would be remiss if we left the dog outside in this heat.
exampleSentences.zh: 如果我們在這種高溫下把狗留在戶外，那就是失職疏忽。

exampleSentences.en: Regulators were remiss in failing to inspect the factory's safety equipment.
exampleSentences.zh: 監管人員未檢查工廠的安全設備，實屬怠忽職守。

remiss.mnemonicHint: re-（往回）＋miss（漏掉）：該做的事反覆 miss 掉，就是「疏忽的」；常見句型 be remiss in doing 表示怠於做某事。

exampleSentences.en: Her cancer has remained in remission for five years.
exampleSentences.zh: 她的癌症已維持緩解狀態五年。

exampleSentences.en: Clinical remission does not necessarily indicate that the underlying disease has been cured.
exampleSentences.zh: 臨床緩解不一定表示潛在疾病已被治癒。

remission.mnemonicHint: re-（往回）＋mission（送出）：症狀像被「送回去」而暫時退去，進入 remission；但緩解不等於完全治癒。

replenished.chinese: 補充；重新裝滿（replenish 的過去式／過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: Sam replenished the bird feeder before leaving for work.
exampleSentences.zh: 山姆上班前補滿了餵鳥器。

exampleSentences.en: Seasonal rainfall replenished the reservoirs after a prolonged drought.
exampleSentences.zh: 季節性降雨在長期乾旱後重新補充了水庫的蓄水量。

replenished.mnemonicHint: re-（再次）＋plen（滿，聯想到 plenty）＋-ish：讓缺少的東西「再次變滿」，就是 replenish；完成後便是 replenished。

replied.chinese: 回答；回覆（reply 的過去式／過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: Maya replied to my text before the train entered the tunnel.
exampleSentences.zh: 火車進入隧道前，Maya 回覆了我的訊息。

exampleSentences.en: The minister replied that the proposed subsidy would require legislative approval.
exampleSentences.zh: 部長回答說，這項補助提案需要立法機關批准。

replied.mnemonicHint: reply 的 y 遇到過去式字尾 -ed 要變 i，形成 replied；想成「昨天已經回了，所以 y 變 i」。

resides.chinese: 居住；存在於（reside 的第三人稱單數）

exampleSentences.en: Our new dentist resides above the bakery on Pine Street.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們的新牙醫住在松樹街那間麵包店樓上。

exampleSentences.en: Legal authority resides in the elected council rather than the appointed committee.
exampleSentences.zh: 法定權力存在於民選議會，而非受任命的委員會。

resides.mnemonicHint: reside 可拆成 re- 加 side，聯想「固定待在某一 side（地方）」；resides 是主詞為 he、she、it 時加 -s 的形式。

resigns.chinese: 辭職；放棄職位（resign 的第三人稱單數）

exampleSentences.en: Nora resigns from the café next Friday to begin nursing school.
exampleSentences.zh: Nora 下週五會辭去咖啡館的工作，開始就讀護理學校。

exampleSentences.en: A cabinet minister typically resigns when accepting responsibility for a serious policy failure.
exampleSentences.zh: 內閣部長在為嚴重政策失誤承擔責任時，通常會辭職。

resigns.mnemonicHint: resign 裡的 sign 像是在辭呈上簽名；resigns 是第三人稱單數。注意 re-sign 是「再次簽署」，有連字號且意思完全不同。

resonance.chinese: 共鳴；深刻的感染力；共振

exampleSentences.en: That childhood photograph has special resonance for everyone in our family.
exampleSentences.zh: 那張童年照片對我們全家人都有特殊的共鳴。

exampleSentences.en: The novel gained political resonance as public concern about inequality intensified.
exampleSentences.zh: 隨著大眾對不平等的憂慮加深，這本小說產生了政治上的共鳴。

resonance.mnemonicHint: resonance 源自拉丁文 resonare「再次發聲」：聲音在空間回響，觀念也能在人心裡反覆回響，於是產生「共鳴」。

resource.chinese: 資源；可利用的手段或資產

exampleSentences.en: This neighborhood library is a useful resource for parents seeking free tutoring.
exampleSentences.zh: 這間社區圖書館是家長尋找免費家教資源的好去處。

exampleSentences.en: Fresh water becomes a strategic resource when prolonged drought reduces regional supplies.
exampleSentences.zh: 長期乾旱使區域供水減少時，淡水便成為戰略資源。

resource.mnemonicHint: re- 有「再次」之意，source 是「來源」；能一再從來源取用的東西就是 resource「資源」。別和 recourse「求助途徑」混淆。

restoration.chinese: 修復；復原；恢復原狀或原位

exampleSentences.en: Careful restoration revealed the original blue paint beneath the cabinet's dark varnish.
exampleSentences.zh: 細心修復後，櫥櫃深色清漆下原本的藍色油漆顯露出來。

exampleSentences.en: Wetland restoration can reduce flood damage while rebuilding habitats for native species.
exampleSentences.zh: 濕地復育能在重建本土物種棲地的同時降低洪災損失。

restoration.mnemonicHint: restore 是 re-「回到」加 store「保存」：把受損事物帶回保存良好的狀態；再加 -ation 就是修復這個過程。

resuscitation.chinese: 復甦；急救使恢復呼吸或意識

exampleSentences.en: Prompt resuscitation by a lifeguard restored the swimmer's breathing before paramedics arrived.
exampleSentences.zh: 救生員及時施行急救，在救護人員抵達前恢復了游泳者的呼吸。

exampleSentences.en: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation preserves blood flow to vital organs during cardiac arrest.
exampleSentences.zh: 心肺復甦術能在心搏停止期間維持流向重要器官的血液。

resuscitation.mnemonicHint: 詞根 suscit 表示「喚起」，re- 表示「再次」，-ation 表示過程；resuscitation 就是「再次喚起生命跡象」的復甦程序。

retorts.chinese: 反駁；回嘴（retort 的第三人稱單數或複數）

exampleSentences.en: Whenever Leo retorts sharply, his sister pauses instead of continuing the argument.
exampleSentences.zh: 每當 Leo 尖銳回嘴時，他姊姊就會停下來，不再繼續爭論。

exampleSentences.en: The author retorts that economic growth alone cannot measure social well-being.
exampleSentences.zh: 作者反駁說，單靠經濟成長無法衡量社會福祉。

retorts.mnemonicHint: retort 可聯想成把對方的話「扭轉回去」；retorts 作動詞是他／她回嘴，作名詞則是多次尖銳的反駁。

retreats.chinese: 撤退；退縮；隱居處（retreat 的第三人稱單數或複數）

exampleSentences.en: Our timid cat retreats under the sofa whenever the vacuum cleaner starts.
exampleSentences.zh: 每當吸塵器啟動，我們那隻膽小的貓就會躲到沙發下。

exampleSentences.en: As coastal ice retreats, darker ocean water absorbs more solar radiation.
exampleSentences.zh: 隨著沿岸海冰消退，較深色的海水會吸收更多太陽輻射。

retreats.mnemonicHint: retreat 中 re- 有「往回」的感覺，treat 可想成前方的待遇太糟，只好往回撤；retreats 也可能是多個靜修地。

reverting.chinese: 恢復原狀；回到先前狀態（revert 的現在分詞）

exampleSentences.en: After testing the update, Priya is reverting to the stable software version.
exampleSentences.zh: 測試更新後，Priya 正在恢復使用穩定版軟體。

exampleSentences.en: Several schools are reverting to printed examinations after detecting widespread online cheating.
exampleSentences.zh: 發現大規模線上作弊後，數所學校正恢復採用紙本考試。

reverting.mnemonicHint: re- 是「回」，vert 是「轉」；revert 就是「轉回原狀」。標準搭配是 revert to，不必再說 revert back，因為 re- 已含「回去」。

exampleSentences.en: This robust backpack survived three rainy camping trips.
exampleSentences.zh: 這個堅固的背包撐過了三次下雨的露營旅行。

exampleSentences.en: Researchers need robust evidence before drawing causal conclusions.
exampleSentences.zh: 研究人員需要有力的證據，才能得出因果結論。

robust.mnemonicHint: 把 robust 聯想成機器人 robot 加上強壯的 bust：像厚實機器人一樣強健、耐用；研究中的 robust evidence 則是經得起檢驗的有力證據。

exampleSentences.en: Please roll the poster carefully before packing it.
exampleSentences.zh: 打包前請小心地把海報捲起來。

exampleSentences.en: Small droplets roll downhill as gravity overcomes surface resistance.
exampleSentences.zh: 當重力克服表面阻力時，小水滴會向坡下滾動。

roll.mnemonicHint: roll 的兩個 l 像一對輪子，提示物體滾動；紙張跟著轉動會被捲起，因此也能表示捲起或一卷物品。

rolled.chinese: 滾動；捲起；已滾動或捲起的

exampleSentences.en: Maya rolled the blanket into a compact bundle.
exampleSentences.zh: 瑪雅把毯子捲成一個小巧的包裹。

exampleSentences.en: Molten material rolled across the surface and cooled rapidly.
exampleSentences.zh: 熔融物質滾過表面後迅速冷卻。

rolled.mnemonicHint: rolled 是 roll 加過去式字尾 -ed，表示已經滾動或捲起；看到 -ed 就想像一張已被捲好的地圖。

rolling.chinese: 滾動中；起伏的；連續進行的

exampleSentences.en: Tears were rolling down her cheeks after the farewell.
exampleSentences.zh: 告別後，眼淚正沿著她的臉頰滑落。

exampleSentences.en: Across rolling hills, vegetation patterns vary with elevation.
exampleSentences.zh: 在連綿起伏的丘陵間，植被型態會隨海拔而變化。

rolling.mnemonicHint: rolling 是 roll 加 -ing，核心畫面是持續轉動；地形像波浪持續上下延伸時，rolling hills 就是連綿起伏的丘陵。

exampleSentences.en: Our baker serves warm rolls with herb butter.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們的麵包師傅供應搭配香草奶油的溫熱小餐包。

exampleSentences.en: Each marble rolls farther when friction is reduced.
exampleSentences.zh: 當摩擦力降低時，每顆彈珠都會滾得更遠。

rolls.mnemonicHint: rolls 可拆成 roll 加 -s：主詞是 he、she、it 時表示『滾動』，作名詞時則是多個捲狀物或小餐包；別和 roles（角色）混淆。

exampleSentences.en: Leo sarcastically thanked me for spilling coffee on him.
exampleSentences.zh: 里歐挖苦地謝我把咖啡灑在他身上。

exampleSentences.en: The columnist sarcastically praised policies that had clearly failed.
exampleSentences.zh: 該專欄作家諷刺地稱讚那些明顯失敗的政策。

sarcastically.mnemonicHint: sarcasm 是『諷刺』，sarcastic 是『諷刺的』，再加副詞字尾 -ally 就成了『諷刺地』；表面稱讚、實際挖苦是典型語氣。

exampleSentences.en: Nina selectively muted alerts during her evening study session.
exampleSentences.zh: 妮娜在晚間讀書時選擇性地關閉部分通知。

exampleSentences.en: Certain membranes selectively permit small molecules to cross.
exampleSentences.zh: 某些薄膜會選擇性地允許小分子通過。

selectively.mnemonicHint: select 是挑選，selective 是有所選擇的，再加 -ly 變成動作方式：不是全部接受，而是依條件有取捨地處理。

exampleSentences.en: The study app selectively integrates vocabulary quizzes into each review session.
exampleSentences.zh: 這款學習應用程式會在每次複習中選擇性地融入字彙測驗。

exampleSentences.en: Her review selectively integrates findings that support a unified argument.
exampleSentences.zh: 她的文獻回顧選擇性地整合了支持統一論點的研究發現。

selectively integrates.mnemonicHint: 這是副詞 selectively 修飾動詞 integrates 的片語：selectively 表示有取捨地，integrates 表示整合；合起來就是只挑合適部分納入整體。

exampleSentences.en: We felt shocked when the repair bill doubled overnight.
exampleSentences.zh: 修理費一夜之間翻倍時，我們都感到震驚。

exampleSentences.en: Observers were shocked by the sudden collapse of the coalition.
exampleSentences.zh: 觀察人士對聯盟突然瓦解感到震驚。

shocked.mnemonicHint: shock 原指突然衝擊，加 -ed 表示人『受到衝擊』，因此感到震驚；人通常是 shocked，造成震驚的事則是 shocking。

exampleSentences.en: Ella is showing gratitude by writing a thoughtful note.
exampleSentences.zh: 艾拉寫了一張貼心的卡片來表達感激。

exampleSentences.en: Survey results showing regional differences require cautious interpretation.
exampleSentences.zh: 顯示區域差異的調查結果需要謹慎解讀。

showing.mnemonicHint: show 加 -ing 表示正在展示或呈現；showing gratitude 不是把『感謝』拿出來看，而是透過行動表現感激，shown 則是 show 的過去分詞。

exampleSentences.en: A handwritten thank-you note is a warm way of showing gratitude.
exampleSentences.zh: 手寫的感謝卡是表達謝意的溫暖方式。

exampleSentences.en: Showing gratitude strengthens social bonds and encourages reciprocal cooperation.
exampleSentences.zh: 表達感謝能鞏固社會連結，並促進互惠合作。

showing gratitude.mnemonicHint: showing 是「展現」，gratitude 是「感激」；把心裡的感謝展現出來，就是 showing gratitude。

exampleSentences.en: We visited three hillside shrines before lunch.
exampleSentences.zh: 午餐前，我們參觀了三座山坡上的神社。

exampleSentences.en: Archaeologists documented several coastal shrines that once served as centers of ritual exchange.
exampleSentences.zh: 考古學家記錄了數座沿海聖地，它們過去曾是儀式交流的中心。

shrines.mnemonicHint: shrines 是 shrine 的複數；可聯想 shine（發光），供奉燈火閃耀的地方就是神龕，但別漏掉 shrine 中的 r。

social outcast.chinese: 被社會排斥的人；社會棄兒

exampleSentences.en: His classmates treated him like a social outcast after the rumor spread.
exampleSentences.zh: 謠言傳開後，同學們把他當成被排斥的人。

exampleSentences.en: Persistent exclusion can turn a vulnerable adolescent into a social outcast.
exampleSentences.zh: 持續的排擠可能使脆弱的青少年淪為社會棄兒。

social outcast.mnemonicHint: outcast 原意像是被 cast out（丟出去）的人；加上 social，就表示被群體推到社會圈外的人。

exampleSentences.en: Investors can only speculate about why the shop closed so suddenly.
exampleSentences.zh: 投資人只能猜測那家店為何突然歇業。

exampleSentences.en: Researchers should not speculate beyond what the available evidence can substantiate.
exampleSentences.zh: 研究人員不應作出超出現有證據所能證實範圍的推測。

speculate.mnemonicHint: spec- 有「看」的意思；只看到部分線索便往下推想，就是 speculate，結論仍未被證實。

stiffening.chinese: 變硬；僵硬化；正在使更強硬

exampleSentences.en: Cold weather is stiffening the clay before we can shape it.
exampleSentences.zh: 寒冷天氣正使黏土變硬，讓我們來不及塑形。

exampleSentences.en: Repeated exposure to stress may cause a gradual stiffening of arterial walls.
exampleSentences.zh: 反覆承受壓力可能導致動脈壁逐漸硬化。

stiffening.mnemonicHint: stiff（僵硬）加 -en（使變得）再加 -ing（正在進行），所以 stiffening 就是「正在變硬或使變硬」。

exampleSentences.en: Some guests chose tea, while still others ordered lemonade.
exampleSentences.zh: 有些客人選了茶，還有另一些人點了檸檬水。

exampleSentences.en: One group favored centralized control, whereas still others advocated local autonomy.
exampleSentences.zh: 一個群體支持中央集權，然而還有其他群體主張地方自治。

still others.mnemonicHint: 此處 still 不是「靜止」，而是「還、仍然」；still others 就是在已列出的群體之外「還有另一批」。

striven.chinese: 努力過；力求過（strive 的過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: Our volunteers have striven to keep the neighborhood kitchen open.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們的志工一直努力維持社區廚房的營運。

exampleSentences.en: Scientists have long striven to reconcile the competing explanations for this phenomenon.
exampleSentences.zh: 科學家長久以來一直努力調和對此現象彼此競爭的解釋。

striven.mnemonicHint: strive 的三態是 strive–strove–striven；striven 不能單獨當過去式，通常要接 have、has 或 had，如 have striven。

exampleSentences.en: Maya is striving to finish the marathon without stopping.
exampleSentences.zh: 瑪雅正努力不停步地跑完馬拉松。

exampleSentences.en: Emerging economies are striving to expand access to education without widening fiscal deficits.
exampleSentences.zh: 新興經濟體正努力擴大教育機會，同時避免擴大財政赤字。

striving.mnemonicHint: strive 是朝目標奮力前進；加 -ing 表示努力正在持續，像雙手不停向目標伸展。

subordination.chinese: 從屬；次要地位；主從關係

exampleSentences.en: The new manager rejected the subordination of interns to routine errands.
exampleSentences.zh: 新任經理反對把實習生貶為只負責例行跑腿工作。

exampleSentences.en: Excessive subordination of local authorities can weaken their capacity to address regional needs.
exampleSentences.zh: 地方機關過度從屬於上級，可能削弱其因應區域需求的能力。

subordination.mnemonicHint: sub- 是「在下方」，ordin 表示「秩序、層級」；被排在權力秩序下方，就是 subordination。

exampleSentences.en: The bells rang in rapid succession as the parade approached.
exampleSentences.zh: 遊行隊伍接近時，鐘聲接連快速響起。

exampleSentences.en: A rapid succession of visual frames creates the illusion of continuous motion.
exampleSentences.zh: 一連串快速呈現的視覺畫面會產生連續運動的錯覺。

succession.mnemonicHint: suc-（接近、接著）加 cess（走）表示一個接一個跟著走；succession 因而可指接連發生，也可指王位或職位的繼承。

exampleSentences.en: Her weekly update neatly summarizes what our team finished.
exampleSentences.zh: 她的每週更新簡潔總結了團隊完成的工作。

exampleSentences.en: The concluding paragraph accurately summarizes the study's principal findings.
exampleSentences.zh: 結論段落準確概述了該研究的主要發現。

summarizes.mnemonicHint: summary 是「摘要」，加上動詞字尾 -ize 成為 summarize；summarizes 是第三人稱單數，表示主詞把重點濃縮成摘要。

exampleSentences.en: He only skimmed the contract superficially before signing it.
exampleSentences.zh: 他簽約前只是草率地瀏覽了合約。

exampleSentences.en: Researchers who examine the evidence superficially may overlook variables that alter the conclusion.
exampleSentences.zh: 研究人員若只從表面檢視證據，可能會忽略足以改變結論的變項。

superficially.mnemonicHint: superficial 來自 surface「表面」的概念，加 -ly 變成副詞；想像只擦桌面、不清理縫隙，就是 superficially。

exampleSentences.en: During rushed meetings, Leo superficially summarizes each proposal without discussing costs.
exampleSentences.zh: 每逢匆忙的會議，Leo 都只粗略概述各項提案，卻不討論成本。

exampleSentences.en: The abstract superficially summarizes the controversy but omits its historical causes.
exampleSentences.zh: 該摘要僅粗略概述爭議，卻省略了其歷史成因。

superficially summarizes.mnemonicHint: superficially 修飾 summarizes：不是深入分析，而是只把最外層重點縮成摘要；可聯想「只看 surface 就寫 summary」。

than that.chinese: 比那個……（不完整比較片段）

exampleSentences.en: This jacket costs less than that one in the window.
exampleSentences.zh: 這件外套比櫥窗裡那件便宜。

exampleSentences.en: The observed preference for remote work was stronger than that predicted by the initial model.
exampleSentences.zh: 實際觀察到的遠距工作偏好強於初始模型的預測。

than that.mnemonicHint: 這是被截斷的比較結構，不能單獨表意；自然句型要補成 comparative + than that one，或 than that predicted/observed。注意 than 是「比」，then 才是「然後」。

that i.chinese: 那是我……；我所……（不完整子句）

exampleSentences.en: That I forgot your birthday does not mean I do not care.
exampleSentences.zh: 我忘了你的生日並不表示我不在乎。

exampleSentences.en: The committee acknowledged that I had reported the discrepancy before the audit began.
exampleSentences.zh: 委員會承認我在稽核開始前就已通報該差異。

that i.mnemonicHint: 原片段缺少後續謂語，而且英文代名詞 I 永遠大寫；修正時寫成 that I + verb，或讓整個 That I + verb 子句充當主詞。

exampleSentences.en: Two cookies are mine; the others are for the children.
exampleSentences.zh: 兩塊餅乾是我的，其餘的是給孩子們的。

exampleSentences.en: Some participants chose buses, whereas the others favored rail transport.
exampleSentences.zh: 部分參與者選擇公車，其餘的人則偏好鐵路運輸。

the others.mnemonicHint: the 指已知範圍，others 指複數的「其餘者」；the others 就是特定群體中剩下的全部，不同於泛指某些其他人的 others。

exampleSentences.en: Our mechanic performed a thorough inspection before the road trip.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們的技師在公路旅行前做了徹底檢查。

exampleSentences.en: Because the audit was thorough, even minor accounting discrepancies were detected.
exampleSentences.zh: 由於稽核十分詳盡，連細微的會計差異也被查出。

thorough.mnemonicHint: thorough 有「從頭查到尾、不漏角落」的感覺；記住 thorough inspection 是徹底檢查，而 through 是穿過、though 是雖然。

exampleSentences.en: Extra locks thwarted the burglar's attempt to enter our garage.
exampleSentences.zh: 額外的鎖使竊賊闖入車庫的企圖落空。

exampleSentences.en: Transparent procedures can thwart attempts to manipulate the allocation of public funds.
exampleSentences.zh: 透明的程序可以阻止操弄公共資金分配的企圖。

thwart.mnemonicHint: 把 thwart 聯想成一道橫著擋路的木板，使計畫過不去；它不只是延遲，而是讓某人的企圖受阻或失敗。

exampleSentences.en: Maya hopes to be a paramedic after she graduates.
exampleSentences.zh: Maya 希望畢業後成為救護技術員。

exampleSentences.en: The evidence appears to be consistent with the proposed hypothesis.
exampleSentences.zh: 證據似乎與所提出的假設一致。

to be.mnemonicHint: to + be 是不定詞，be 會依主詞和時態變成 am/is/are/was/were；把它視為「要成為或處於某狀態」的基本骨架。

exampleSentences.en: Local athletes meet every morning to strive for better personal records.
exampleSentences.zh: 當地運動員每天早上集合，努力爭取更好的個人紀錄。

exampleSentences.en: To strive for accuracy, researchers must disclose assumptions and replicate key measurements.
exampleSentences.zh: 為追求準確性，研究人員必須揭露假設並重複關鍵測量。

to strive.mnemonicHint: strive 是持續用力追求目標；不定詞 to strive 表示「去努力」。可連結 strove（過去式）與 striven（過去分詞），不要和 thrive「蓬勃發展」混淆。

exampleSentences.en: Please add some lemon to that cup of tea.
exampleSentences.zh: 請在那杯茶裡加一些檸檬。

exampleSentences.en: The committee objected strongly to that interpretation of the survey results.
exampleSentences.zh: 委員會強烈反對那種對調查結果的解讀。

to that.mnemonicHint: to 表示方向或關聯，that 指已提過的事物；兩者合用必須接在動詞或名詞後，不能當成獨立單字，例如 object to that interpretation（反對那種解讀）。

exampleSentences.en: This is the address to which you should send the package.
exampleSentences.zh: 這就是你應該寄送包裹的地址。

exampleSentences.en: Researchers identified the conditions to which the organism was most sensitive.
exampleSentences.zh: 研究人員找出了該生物最敏感的環境條件。

to which.mnemonicHint: to 提到關係方向，which 回指前面的名詞；正式關係子句把介系詞提前形成 to which，口語則常說 which ... to。它不是完整句子，需搭配先行詞與子句。

exampleSentences.en: She stored the treasurable family letters in a fireproof box.
exampleSentences.zh: 她把那些值得珍藏的家書收藏在防火箱裡。

exampleSentences.en: The archivist considered the diary treasurable because no other firsthand account had survived.
exampleSentences.zh: 由於沒有其他第一手紀錄留存，檔案管理員認為這本日記值得珍藏。

treasurable.mnemonicHint: treasure（珍寶、珍藏）加 -able（值得……的）就是「值得珍藏的」。此字正確但較罕見；日常英文通常用 precious 或 treasured，別誤寫成 treasureable。

exampleSentences.en: Maya turned down the music when her baby fell asleep.
exampleSentences.zh: 寶寶睡著後，瑪雅把音樂音量調低了。

exampleSentences.en: Several qualified applicants were turned down because the program had limited funding.
exampleSentences.zh: 由於該計畫經費有限，數名合格申請者遭到拒絕。

turned down.mnemonicHint: turn down 可把東西「往下轉」而調低音量，也可把提議「往下壓」而拒絕；turned down 是其過去式或過去分詞，需依受詞判斷是哪個意思。

exampleSentences.en: Our mediator stayed unbiased during the dispute between the neighbors.
exampleSentences.zh: 我們的調解人在鄰居之間的爭端中保持公正。

exampleSentences.en: An unbiased sample is essential for drawing valid conclusions about the population.
exampleSentences.zh: 無偏差的樣本是對母體得出有效結論的必要條件。

unbiased.mnemonicHint: un-（不）加 biased（有偏見的）就是「沒有偏向」。想像天平沒有倒向任何一邊；unbiased 是形容詞，不是動詞。

exampleSentences.en: After camping all weekend, Leo looked tired and unkempt.
exampleSentences.zh: 露營了一整個週末後，里歐看起來疲憊又不修邊幅。

exampleSentences.en: The witness described an unkempt man wearing a torn gray coat.
exampleSentences.zh: 目擊者描述一名衣著不整、穿著破舊灰色外套的男子。

unkempt.mnemonicHint: kempt 是「整理好的」，前加 un- 就變成「沒整理的」；常形容凌亂的頭髮、衣著或外表，拼字不要誤作 unkept。

exampleSentences.en: One careless click unleashed dozens of balloons across the room.
exampleSentences.zh: 一次不小心的點擊讓數十顆氣球飛散到整個房間。

exampleSentences.en: Rapid deregulation unleashed competitive forces that transformed the telecommunications industry.
exampleSentences.zh: 快速解除管制釋放了競爭力量，進而改變電信產業。

unleashed.mnemonicHint: leash 是牽繩，un-leash 就是解開牽繩、讓力量衝出去；unleashed 可作 unleash 的過去式，也可形容已被釋放或引爆的力量。

unsanctioned.chinese: 未經批准的；未獲授權的

exampleSentences.en: Two students organized an unsanctioned concert in the dormitory lounge.
exampleSentences.zh: 兩名學生在宿舍交誼廳舉辦了一場未經批准的演唱會。

exampleSentences.en: Officials warned that unsanctioned data collection could violate research ethics standards.
exampleSentences.zh: 官員警告，未經授權的資料蒐集可能違反研究倫理標準。

unsanctioned.mnemonicHint: un-（未）加 sanctioned（獲正式批准的）表示「未獲批准」。sanction 本身也可指制裁，但 unsanctioned 在此針對的是缺少官方許可。

exampleSentences.en: Hang the mirror vertically beside the narrow bookshelf.
exampleSentences.zh: 把鏡子垂直掛在窄書架旁邊。

exampleSentences.en: A vertical line on the graph represents the rate of population growth.
exampleSentences.zh: 圖表上的垂直線代表人口成長率。

vertical.mnemonicHint: vert- 有「轉、朝向」的詞根意象；vertical 就像從地面直直朝天空延伸。可聯想座標圖的 vertical axis 是上下方向，與 horizontal 相反。

exampleSentences.en: What if the last bus leaves before we reach the station?
exampleSentences.zh: 如果我們抵達車站前末班車就開走了，該怎麼辦？

exampleSentences.en: Economists asked, "What if consumer demand remains weak despite lower interest rates?"
exampleSentences.zh: 經濟學家提出：「如果降息後消費需求仍然疲弱，情況會如何？」

what if.mnemonicHint: what（什麼結果）加 if（如果）用來提出假設或擔憂，相當於「如果……會怎樣？」作名詞修飾語時要加連字號，如 a what-if scenario。

which affect.chinese: 影響……的（關係子句片段；接複數先行詞時合乎文法）

exampleSentences.en: These are the habits which affect my sleep the most.
exampleSentences.zh: 這些就是最影響我睡眠的習慣。

exampleSentences.en: Researchers identified several variables which affect the accuracy of the forecasting model.
exampleSentences.zh: 研究人員找出數個會影響預測模型準確度的變數。

which affect.mnemonicHint: 這是從句片段，不宜單獨背；which 後面的 affect 要和先行詞一致：複數 variables which affect，單數 variable which affects。affect 多作動詞「影響」，effect 多作名詞「效果」。

who interested.chinese: 有興趣的人（非標準片段）

exampleSentences.en: Anyone who is interested can join our pottery class tonight.
exampleSentences.zh: 任何有興趣的人今晚都可以參加我們的陶藝課。

exampleSentences.en: Applicants who are interested in the fellowship must submit two recommendation letters.
exampleSentences.zh: 有意申請該獎學金者必須繳交兩封推薦信。

who interested.mnemonicHint: who interested 少了 be 動詞；說「有興趣的人」要用 who is interested（單數）或 who are interested（複數）。別和 who is interesting「很有趣的人」混淆。

exampleSentences.en: Dinner will be ready in about twenty minutes.
exampleSentences.zh: 晚餐大約二十分鐘後會準備好。

exampleSentences.en: The revised policy will be effective at the beginning of the next fiscal year.
exampleSentences.zh: 修訂後的政策將於下一個會計年度開始時生效。

will be.mnemonicHint: will 把時間推向未來，be 表示「是／處於」；合起來就是「未來將是某種狀態」。後面可接名詞、形容詞或地點，如 will be a leader、ready、at home。

exampleSentences.en: My old hiking boots look worn but still feel comfortable.
exampleSentences.zh: 我的舊登山靴看起來很磨損，但穿起來仍然舒服。

exampleSentences.en: Frequent traffic had worn a deep groove into the ancient stone steps.
exampleSentences.zh: 頻繁的人流已在古老石階上磨出一道深溝。

worn.mnemonicHint: wear–wore–worn 是「穿戴／磨損」的不規則三態；把 worn 想成鞋底紋路被磨平，既能表示「穿過的」，也能表示「磨損的」。

exampleSentences.en: After carrying boxes upstairs, I felt completely worn out.
exampleSentences.zh: 把箱子搬上樓後，我感到筋疲力盡。

exampleSentences.en: The turbine blades were worn out by repeated thermal cycles and required replacement.
exampleSentences.zh: 渦輪葉片因反覆的熱循環而耗損，必須更換。

worn out.mnemonicHint: wear out 是把耐用度一路「穿到外面都沒了」；人被耗盡就是筋疲力竭，物品被耗盡就是磨壞。worn out 可作形容詞，wore out 則是過去式動作。

exampleSentences.en: A quieter table would be better for our conversation.
exampleSentences.zh: 較安靜的桌位會更適合我們談話。

exampleSentences.en: Without adequate controls, the experiment would be vulnerable to sampling bias.
exampleSentences.zh: 若缺乏適當控制，這項實驗就容易受到抽樣偏誤影響。

would be.mnemonicHint: would 是 will 往後退一步：可能是條件假設、較委婉語氣，或從過去看未來；would be 因此常譯為「會是／本來會是」，語氣不像 will be 那麼確定。

would have.chinese: 本來會……；原本可能會……（後接過去分詞）

exampleSentences.en: Without your reminder, I would have missed the dentist appointment.
exampleSentences.zh: 若不是你提醒，我本來會錯過牙醫預約。

exampleSentences.en: Under stricter assumptions, the proposed estimator would have produced substantially different results.
exampleSentences.zh: 在更嚴格的假設下，所提出的估計量本來會產生大不相同的結果。

would have.mnemonicHint: would have + 過去分詞把「會」放進未實現的過去：would have missed 是「本來會錯過」。口語縮寫 would've 聽似 would of，但正確拼法永遠是 would have。
